domainReasonVocabulary.owner: DELIVERY request-rejection detail; these are not D9 HostTermination codes

v1PlanIntentOverlay.input: The exact frozen C-2 PlanIntent after schema/profile validation and before attempt-admission. Walk axisOrder exactly. For scalar axes inspect the one value; for collection axes inspect C-2's already-canonical committed order. ALLOW continues, DENY returns immediately, and ALLOW_IF evaluates its named condition immediately and returns that condition's onFalse denial when false. A stored-view intent has no analysis payload and is admitted to the separate C-2 stored-read join.

allowed-fact-stage-grant.rule: The grantId is referenced by at least one stage and every reference is from an otherwise-v1-allowed fact-derivation stage. Unreferenced grants and references from a rule, policy or Probe stage reject.

bundled-host-builtin.rule: The contribution origin is bundled and its artifact is part of the selected signed host release; tracked-project or external host-builtin code is not a host builtin.

bundled-provider-process-grant.rule: The grantId is referenced by at least one fact-derivation semantic-provider stage and every reference names a bundled providerId in the exact set [rust-semantic, typescript-semantic].

bundled-semantic-provider.rule: The contribution origin is bundled, authority is semantic-provider, and contributionId is exactly rust-semantic or typescript-semantic. Every referencing stage carries the same providerId.

bundled-semantic-provider-stage.rule: providerId is exactly rust-semantic or typescript-semantic and resolves to one matching contribution that passes bundled-semantic-provider. Its relations are a non-empty subset of that provider's exact selected capability-manifest relation/rung map; a provider label cannot claim an unsupported relation.

rust-repository-execution.rule: Exactly one capability=repository-execution grant exists for scope.projectId, is referenced by a fact-derivation semantic-provider stage whose providerId and matching bundled contributionId are rust-semantic, and has parameters exactly {build-scripts:<bool>,network:false,procedural-macros:<bool>} matching the two repositoryExecution grant flags. networkIntent is denied; compilerPlugins and projectHooks are disabled. The grant is never global or inherited.

rejectionProjection.reasonRule: Every DENY or failed ALLOW_IF returns its exact domainReasonCode as typed detail; it never becomes a D9 code.

fixtureModel.mutationLanguage: Apply ordered set/remove JSON-pointer operations to baseAllowedAnalysisIntent; every resulting intent must independently validate under live C-2 before the overlay result is asserted.

v1PlanIntentOverlayCommitment.canonicalization: UTF-8 JSON with object keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace, Unicode emitted directly; the v1PlanIntentOverlay object only

admissionRule.evaluationPoint: request-validation after C-2 schema validation/profile expansion/PlanIntent freeze and before attempt-admission

externalScannerOverlay.inputRepresentation: The fully profile-expanded, normalized and frozen pre-admission PlanIntent while still at request-validation. Its planIntentCommitment is SHA-256 over canonical JSON v1 under domain opensip.plan-intent.v1; rejection inspects the committed object, never a later ExecutionPlan reconstruction.

selector.providerIdRule: providerId is required on the matching stage intent
selector.consistencyRule: A stage intent and its referenced contribution must agree; either external-scanner surface is sufficient to reject and disagreement is invalid PlanIntent.

externalScannerOverlay.decisionPoint: request-validation after C-2 schema validation and before attempt-admission
externalScannerOverlay.nonEquivalence: This is a v1 product-scope overlay, not an ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT or restricted-runtime failure. C-2 continues to recognize external-scanner as a valid supervised-implementation-effect operator for a future slice.

blockers.externalScanner: explicit future product-slice decision plus a separately reviewed scanner authority/delivery contract

terminationIntegration.rule: DELIVERY owns domain conditions; D9 exclusively owns public host-termination classes and codes. A DELIVERY spelling outside D9's closed vocabulary is a contract defect, never a new implementation-local code.

providerProtocolFault.deliveryCondition: The bundled provider violates framing, integrity, handshake or closed protocol semantics.

excludedCapabilityForm.projectionRule: The domainReasonCode remains typed explanatory detail in the rejection body; D9's errorCode is the sole public host-termination code. Probe or imperative admission does not mint a second termination vocabulary.

excludedExternalScanner.projectionRule: The domainReasonCode explains the v1 product overlay and is not a new D9 code. D9's existing rejection cause and errorCode remain the sole public host-termination vocabulary.

providerAvailability.deliveryCondition: A correctly framed provider response declares that the selected semantic universe is unavailable before emitting any admitted fact batch.
providerAvailability.projectionRule: The host records Coverage and may seal a coherent terminal Run; requiredness determines whether the verdict is indeterminate. Availability is not a provider protocol fault.

providerBudget.deliveryCondition: A correctly framed provider response exhausts its deterministic work-unit budget.

providerDeliveryFailure.deliveryCondition: A signed profile promises the bundled provider/runtime closure but an exact executable or pinned payload cannot be opened, verified or spawned.

providerInterruption.deliveryCondition: The finite host receives SIGINT or SIGTERM before finalization and cancels/terminates its provider child.
providerInterruption.projectionRule: A user signal is not relabelled as a provider crash or protocol violation; D9 finalization ordering remains authoritative.

rustSemanticSubstrate.why: The product promises compiler-grade Rust resolution, not editor convenience. rustc_driver exposes the compiler phases and queries needed for exact resolved/type/call facts; the interface is explicitly unstable, so instability is contained behind a versioned provider process and an exactly pinned toolchain rather than leaked into the host.
rustSemanticSubstrate.processModel: One supervised provider process per Rust semantic universe. It is a TCB-accepted compiler process and a fault-containment boundary, not a security sandbox. It never runs in the lifetime-neutral pure core.

providerProtocol.transport: length-delimited canonical CBOR over inherited stdin/stdout
providerProtocol.frameIntegrity: uint64 big-endian length plus sha256 payload digest; an incomplete or extra frame is D9 PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (faultCause provider-protocol)
providerProtocol.ownership: Internal worker protocol for the bundled provider; version still enters the release manifest and PlanId because it changes facts.

toolchainIdentity: rustc verbose version and host triple
offlineAssets: rustc-dev/LLVM libraries required by the driver
standard-library source metadata needed by analysis

repositoryExecution.withoutGrant: Do not execute build scripts, procedural macros, compiler plugins or project hooks. Any relation whose universe depends on generated cfg reports Coverage unavailable/provider-unavailable.
repositoryExecution.withGrant: A per-project execution-capable-resolution grant may run build scripts and procedural macros with network disabled. The grant, generated cfg corpus, tool paths and output digests enter PlanId.
repositoryExecution.inheritance: Never global and never inherited by another ProjectId.

rustSemanticSubstrate.upgradeRule: A rustc commit change is a provider/semantic-universe change and follows detector-pivot/versioning rules; it is never a transparent patch.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: The public editor protocol does not bind the complete compiler fact/cfg universe required by P-4, and server state would become an undeclared evidence authority.
Compiler instability, process authority and crash fate would cross the pure-core boundary.

typescriptSemanticSubstrate.executionBoundary: The Rust orchestration host directly spawns the bundled Node.js executable as a private one-shot worker process and passes the bundled provider entry point as its only script. TypeScript compiler code is never embedded in the Rust host and a system Node.js, PATH lookup, package-manager resolution, language server or resident daemon is never used.

processModel.hostLifetime: The v1 orchestration host is one-shot.
processModel.start: Spawn only after SnapshotId, PlanId and the complete TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey have been bound by the host.
processModel.end: After exactly one terminal Complete, Unavailable or BudgetExhausted response, close the protocol, wait for clean child exit, then destroy its scratch directory. A child is never retained for a later request.

packaging.runtime: A platform-specific Node.js executable and its required shared runtime payload, installed from the signed release closure.
packaging.provider: A platform-neutral JavaScript worker entry point, one exact TypeScript compiler payload, the exact TypeScript standard-library declaration corpus, closed identity descriptors, and license/notice files.
releaseManifestEdges: typescript-deep and full profiles include both artifacts
the artifact sha256 and byte length in ReleaseManifestV1 pin the complete bytes; no semver range or mutable package resolution is permitted
packaging.launch: The host resolves both artifacts through the active signed manifest, verifies their already-installed exact digests, and invokes the absolute bundled runtime path with argv [absolute-bundled-node, --no-addons, absolute-bundled-provider-entry]. It does not invoke a shell, consult PATH/NODE_PATH/NODE_OPTIONS, or execute npm, npx, pnpm, yarn, bun or deno.

identity.versionSelectionRule: A release selects exactly one Node.js runtime payload and exactly one TypeScript compiler payload. The architecture does not freeze one numerical version forever; the signed release descriptors do. Ranges, system-runtime substitution and install-time re-resolution are forbidden.

runtimeDescriptor.binding: The descriptor is inside the signed typescript-runtime artifact; its bytes and every named payload are covered by that artifact's ReleaseManifestV1 sha256.

providerDescriptor.binding: The descriptor, compiler JavaScript, standard-library corpus and exact default work-budget profile are inside the signed typescript-provider artifact; no npm registry or host installation participates.

defaultWorkBudgetProfile.binding: The provider descriptor names this exact profileId and digest; both fields are repeated in HelloAckV1 and compared before source bytes. Because providerDescriptorSha256 is a TypeScript semantic-universe component, the profile is PlanId-bound without adding an ambient default.

identity.hostValidation: Before sending source bytes, the host compares every handshake identity with the two verified descriptors and rejects any mismatch as provider-protocol.
identity.planIdRule: PlanId commits manifestId, selected capabilityManifestId, TypeScript provider/runtime artifact IDs and sha256 values, both identity-descriptor sha256 values, protocolMajor, providerBuildId, Node/V8/modules ABI identity, TypeScript version/compiler digest/stdlib Merkle root, the descriptor-bound defaultWorkBudgetProfileId/defaultWorkBudgetProfileSha256, platformId, and the complete resolved-inputs TypeScript semantic-universe components. A change to any one creates a different TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey and PlanId.
identity.releaseRule: G16 must exercise the exact descriptor pair named by every supported platform/profile release row; a descriptor mismatch, missing field or substituted runtime blocks release.

offlineAssets.activationRule: Every required asset is inside the signed exact artifact closure and digest-verified before spawn. Missing, extra-runtime-substituted or network-fetched assets are forbidden.

providerProtocol.transport: bidirectional inherited pipes: length-delimited canonical CBOR on stdin/stdout

canonicalCbor.mapOrder: ascending lexicographic order of each key's deterministic-CBOR encoded bytes
canonicalCbor.decodeRule: Decode once under the closed payload schema. Duplicate, missing, unknown, mistyped, out-of-range or non-canonical values are provider-protocol; no ignore-unknown or last-key-wins behavior exists.

limits.limitRule: A declared length/count above its limit is rejected before allocation; cumulative counts are checked for uint64 overflow. Limits are protocol safety bounds, not semantic budgets.

fields.frameType: text; exact member of the direction's closed frame vocabulary
fields.sequence: uint64; independent per direction, starts at 0 and increments by 1

definitions.ExecutionId: canonical host-allocated ExecutionId text; exact equality with AttemptRecord
definitions.SnapshotId: canonical sealed SnapshotId text; exact equality with ExecutionPlan.snapshotId
definitions.PlanId: text matching ^plan1:sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$; already host-recomputed and verified

fields.path: non-empty normalized project-relative NFC text; entries sorted by UTF-8 bytes and unique
fields.byteLength: uint64; file byte length, zero for symlink
fields.contentSha256: DigestHex for file bytes; null for symlink
fields.linkTarget: normalized sealed link-target text for symlink; null for file

fields.sourceFilesVisited: uint64 maximum; increment once on first compiler-host open of a distinct canonical source path
fields.astNodesVisited: uint64 maximum; increment once when a TypeScript AST node is first entered for this stage
fields.moduleResolutionQueries: uint64 maximum; increment once per canonical (containingFile,moduleSpecifier,mode) resolver query
fields.typeQueries: uint64 maximum; increment once per TypeChecker query issued by this stage
fields.factBytesEmitted: uint64 maximum sum of deterministic-CBOR FactCandidateV1 byte lengths

ProviderWorkBudgetV1.zeroRule: zero permits zero corresponding operations; there is no unlimited sentinel
ProviderWorkBudgetV1.authoritativeSource: stageRequestProjection.budgetProjection: an admitted C-2 work-units limit maps to all six maxima; otherwise the signed TypeScript provider budget profile supplies the exact defaults. The projected six-field object is sent on the wire and is the sole semantic-budget authority.

fields.dependsOn: sorted unique array of exact C-2 stageId text; absent C-2 dependsOn normalizes to [], present dependsOn is copied exactly
fields.relations: non-empty sorted unique array; every value exists in live fact-plane relationRegistry and equals this C-2 stage's relation set
fields.requestedCoverageDomain: host-constructed RequestedCoverageDomainV1; the worker returns exactly one CoverageResultV1 per full requested key

fields.path: exact canonical path of one SnapshotManifestV1 file entry

SnapshotFileSubjectV1.ordering: strict ascending path UTF-8 bytes; paths unique

fields.subjectCount: uint64 exact number of SnapshotManifestV1 entries whose kind=file

SubjectScopeV1.membershipRule: The subject set is exactly every kind=file entry already supplied in SnapshotManifestV1. Both sides reconstruct the sorted SnapshotFileSubjectV1 array from the sealed manifest, verify subjectCount and commitment, and therefore can prove membership and non-membership without repeating file rows in Analyze.

fields.keys: non-empty sorted unique array of full CoverageKeyV1; length <= maxRequestedCoverageKeysPerStage
fields.domainCommitment: Sha256Text = SHA-256(UTF8('opensip.ts-provider.requested-coverage-domain.v1') || 0x00 || deterministic-CBOR({subjectScope,keys})); domainCommitment itself is excluded from the preimage

RequestedCoverageDomainV1.workerRule: Before analysis the worker recomputes subjectScope and domainCommitment, requires every key.subjectScopeCommitment to equal subjectScope.subjectScopeCommitment, and rejects missing, duplicate, unordered, unrequested or non-canonical keys as provider-protocol.

AnchorRefV1.join: field-for-field exact transport implementation of fact-plane.v1.json#factRecordContractV1.anchorSchema (opensip.anchor-ref.v1); source-span values use opensip.source-span.v1

variants.source-span: kind=source-span; snapshotId/path/contentSha256/startByte/endByte present; factId=null; [startByte,endByte) lies within the sealed file bytes
variants.fact-ref: kind=fact-ref; factId is a canonical already-admitted fact identity; snapshotId/path/contentSha256/startByte/endByte are null

AnchorRefV1.ordering: anchors are sorted by deterministic-CBOR bytes and duplicates are rejected

fields.candidateOrdinal: uint64 contiguous within its stage across FactBatch frames
fields.relation: live fact-plane relationRegistry key requested by the attributed stage
fields.resolution: a rung of that relation's live ladder
fields.layer: the relation's exact live fact-plane layer; for this provider normally semantic or derived
fields.producerVersion: exact providerBuildId from the verified handshake
fields.targetUniverseId: canonical target universe text; required for every fact
fields.confidenceMillionths: uint64 0..1000000; host projects exact rational value/1000000 to fact-plane confidence
fields.relationSchemaId: exact host-owned schemaId selected from fact-plane.v1.json#factRecordContractV1.relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1.schemas[relation] at schemaVersion; provider-local names are invalid
fields.canonicalRelationPayload: deterministic-CBOR byte string conforming byte-for-byte to that host registry schema, at most maxFactCandidatePayloadBytes

FactCandidateV1.hostJoin: This transport object is exactly opensip.fact-candidate.v1 and is never an admitted fact. Under opensip.fact-candidate-admission.v1 the Rust host validates the host-owned opensip.relation-payload-registry.v1 schema and opensip.anchor-ref.v1 anchors, injects the verified SnapshotId, constructs opensip.fact-record.v1, and alone computes/verifies opensip.fact-id.v1 before admission. candidateOrdinal, RequestId, ExecutionId, stage/batch order and arrival order never enter FACT-ID-V1.

CoverageKeyV1.join: Field-for-field exact implementation of c2-plan-stage-schema.v3.json#coverageKey.key; relation/rung are cross-checked against live fact-plane.

fields.targetUniverseId: canonical target universe text; mandatory, including cross-universe relations
fields.subjectScopeCommitment: Sha256Text commitment to the exact examined subject set

fields.entryOrdinal: uint64 contiguous within the stage Coverage array
fields.deficiency: null exactly when coverageState=complete; otherwise one live fact-plane deficiency value

CoverageResultV1.completenessRule: For every full CoverageKeyV1 in the attributed stage's requestedCoverageDomain.keys there is exactly one entry, in the same order, committing the exhaustive examined subject/target partition. Missing, duplicate or unrequested keys are provider-protocol.

fields.factCommitment: Sha256Text over this stage's ordered FactCandidateV1 stream
fields.coverageCommitment: Sha256Text over this stage's ordered CoverageResultV1 stream

fields.limits: closed map equal to wireSchema.limits numeric fields

fields.defaultWorkBudgetProfileId: exact text typescript-provider-default-work-budget-v1 from the verified provider descriptor
fields.defaultWorkBudgetProfileSha256: DigestHex; exact bf7305a12d26a1938b615c861f995d66eac494915e6140c4942a2ea6f0846da6 from the verified provider descriptor

fields.entries: sorted unique array of SnapshotEntryV1, length <= maxSnapshotEntries

fields.byteOffset: uint64 exact cumulative prior chunk bytes

fields.stageRequests: non-empty array of StageRequestV1, length <= maxAnalyzeStages

fields.facts: non-empty ordered array of FactCandidateV1, length <= maxFactBatchFacts

fields.entries: non-empty ordered array containing exactly one CoverageResultV1 per full key in this stage's requestedCoverageDomain.keys, in key order; length <= maxCoverageEntriesPerFrame

fields.affectedStageIds: all requested stageIds in request order
fields.coverage: ordered stage-major array containing exactly one CoverageResultV1 per full key in every requestedCoverageDomain.keys; coverageState=unknown and deficiency=provider-unavailable

fields.observed: uint64 first disallowed count; exactly limit+1
fields.coverage: ordered stage-major array containing exactly one CoverageResultV1 per full key in every requestedCoverageDomain.keys; coverageState=unknown and deficiency=budget-exhausted

fields.stageResults: array of StageResultV1 exactly one per requested stage in request order
fields.factStreamCommitment: Sha256Text over every ordered FactCandidateV1 from all stages
fields.coverageStreamCommitment: Sha256Text over every ordered CoverageResultV1 from all stages

fields.executionId: exact OpenUniverse ExecutionId if opened, otherwise null

multiStageAnalyze.selection: Analyze.stageRequests contains all and only C-2 fact-derivation stages in the verified ExecutionPlan whose operator=semantic-provider, providerId=typescript-semantic and selected semantic universe equals OpenUniverse.universeKey.
multiStageAnalyze.batchability: The selected stages must be dependency-batchable: every dependency outside the selected set has completed before Analyze, intra-set dependencies point to an earlier stageRequest, and no dependency path leaves the set and later re-enters it. Otherwise the host rejects the ExecutionPlan before provider spawn as a Plan validation error.
multiStageAnalyze.ordering: stageRequests preserve the verified ExecutionPlan's declared logical order and carry contiguous stageOrdinal. stageId/operator/providerId/relations are copied exactly; absent dependsOn becomes []; budget and requestedCoverageDomain are produced only by stageRequestProjection. The worker cannot add, omit, merge or reorder stages, relations or requested Coverage keys.
multiStageAnalyze.attribution: Every FactBatch and Coverage names exactly one current stageId. Candidate ordinals and batch indices are contiguous. Output for a later stage before the current stage's Coverage is provider-protocol.
multiStageAnalyze.completeness: Complete.stageResults is a bijection with stageRequests and its counts/commitments must reproduce the observed streams. Complete means protocol completion, while each CoverageResultV1 independently states semantic completeness/deficiency.
multiStageAnalyze.atomicity: All stage streams form one Analyze transaction. Nothing is admitted until Complete+zero-exit+EOF; Unavailable, BudgetExhausted, Cancelled or fault discards every candidate fact from every stage.

stageRequestProjection.sourceContract: resolved-inputs.v2.json#planIdContract.planDescriptorSchema.workflow, which is exact structural equality with the frozen C-2 PlanIntent admissionDescriptor.workflow and has already passed the total DELIVERY v1 overlay
stageRequestProjection.selectedInput: each and only dependency-batchable fact-derivation stage whose operator=semantic-provider and providerId=typescript-semantic, in verified ExecutionPlan logical order

fieldProjection.stageOrdinal: zero-based position in the selected logical order
fieldProjection.dependsOn: if stage.dependsOn is absent emit []; otherwise copy the already-canonical sorted unique array exactly
fieldProjection.relations: copy the already-canonical non-empty stage.relations exactly; each relation/rung is resolved through coverageDomain.relationResolutionById
fieldProjection.budget: apply budgetProjection exactly; no global budget, ambient setting, wall clock or worker-chosen default participates
fieldProjection.requestedCoverageDomain: apply coverageDomain exactly before provider spawn

work-units.rule: For {unit:work-units,limit:L}, emit each of the six ProviderWorkBudgetV1 dimensions with the exact uint64 value L. Counters are independent ceilings; exhaustion of any one terminates the whole Analyze.

budgetProjection.unsupportedUnitFate: milliseconds, bytes and items are rejected by v1PlanIntentOverlay.typescriptStageBudgetUnit during request-validation with FEATURE.TYPESCRIPT_STAGE_BUDGET_UNIT_NOT_IN_V1; they never reach PlanId, StageRequest projection or provider spawn
budgetProjection.soleAuthority: The emitted six-field budget is the sole worker budget. AdmissionDescriptor.budgets, environment, elapsed time and provider heuristics cannot replace or scale it.

coverageDomain.authority: The Rust host derives and sends the complete requested key domain. The worker reports results against that domain and has no authority to infer, narrow, expand or repartition it.

subjectScope.membership: exactly every kind=file SnapshotManifestV1 entry, including non-TypeScript files; file-kind classification is already sealed and no extension heuristic changes membership
subjectScope.canonicalMembers: SnapshotFileSubjectV1 rows sorted by path UTF-8 bytes
subjectScope.reconstruction: host and worker independently reconstruct the same member array from the accepted sealed manifest before Analyze

coverageDomain.relationSource: the exact typescript-semantic relation/rung map in the selected signed install-profile capability manifest; a stage relation outside this map is denied by bundled-semantic-provider-stage

targetPartition.intraUniverse: For a relation absent from live C-2 coverageKey.crossUniverseRelations, emit exactly one key whose targetUniverseId equals OpenUniverse.universeKey.
targetPartition.crossUniverse: For imports, calls or references, emit exactly one key for every activated PlanDescriptorV1.semanticUniverses entry, including the TypeScript source universe, using that entry's provider-specific recomputed universe key as targetUniverseId.
targetPartition.canonicalOrder: activated semantic universes are unique by providerId and limited in v1 to rust-semantic and typescript-semantic; target keys are then included in the final deterministic-CBOR key sort

keyConstruction.ordering: sort full CoverageKeyV1 maps by ascending deterministic-CBOR bytes and reject duplicates

cardinality.formula: sum over stage.relations of (activated semantic-universe count for cross-universe relation, otherwise 1)
cardinality.perFullKey: exactly one CoverageResultV1 for each full requested key; never one per bare relation
cardinality.bounds: maxRelationsPerStage=64 multiplied by maxActivatedSemanticUniversesV1=2 gives at most 128 requested keys, equal to maxRequestedCoverageKeysPerStage and below maxCoverageEntriesPerFrame=4096
cardinality.normalSuccess: the stage's single CoverageV1.entries is a positional bijection with requestedCoverageDomain.keys; each entry repeats the identical full key
cardinality.failureTerminal: UnavailableV1 and BudgetExhaustedV1 flatten stages in Analyze.stageRequests order and keys in each requestedCoverageDomain.keys order; each result has that stageId and a per-stage entryOrdinal starting at zero

coverageDomain.validation: The host verifies the worker's domain and result bijections before admitting Coverage. A missing, duplicate, unordered, altered or unrequested key is provider-protocol / PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION; no partial domain is admitted.

overflowFate.arithmetic: Use checked uint64 add/multiply before allocation; never wrap, truncate, sample, chunk away or spawn the provider on failure.
overflowFate.trigger: any checked-arithmetic overflow or derived key count greater than maxRequestedCoverageKeysPerStage
overflowFate.classification: host invariant failure after admitted v1 validation
overflowFate.proof: Under the closed v1 provider set and declared wire limits the count is <=128; reaching this branch proves a host/contract implementation defect, not user budget exhaustion or provider unavailability.

vectors.mutation: duplicate keyIndex 0 in a Coverage response
append a third targetUniverseId not present in requestedCoverageDomain.keys
reverse the two keys before sending Analyze
vectors.expected: host invariant failure / SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE before provider spawn

vectors.mutation: force checked derivedKeyCount=129 or a checked uint64 arithmetic overflow
vectors.expected: operational-failed / SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE before provider spawn; no truncation and no Coverage

commitments.domainRule: Each commitment is SHA-256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || deterministic-CBOR(value)) and rendered sha256:<64 lowercase hex>.
commitments.empty: An empty fact stream is committed as the deterministic-CBOR empty array under the applicable domain; it is never omitted. Coverage is never empty for a requested stage.

wireSchemaCommitment.canonicalization: UTF-8 JSON with object keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace, Unicode emitted directly; the wireSchema object only

canonicalProviderIdJoin.joinRule: The exact C-2 full-profile fixture must validate and ALLOW under the DELIVERY overlay; its two canonical provider IDs must equal the two RI semanticUniverses provider IDs and the selected DELIVERY capability-manifest provider IDs. The TypeScript selector must select s3 without aliasing or renaming.

providerProtocol.frameIntegrity: Each frame is uint64 big-endian payload length, 32 raw SHA-256 payload bytes, then one canonical-CBOR payload. EOF before a terminal response, digest mismatch, non-canonical CBOR, unknown/duplicate/out-of-order frame, frame after terminal response, or any non-frame stdout byte is provider-protocol and maps to PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

ordering.stageOrder: Analyze.stageRequests order; each requested stage emits zero or more contiguous FactBatch frames with batchIndex 0..n-1, then exactly one Coverage frame, before the next stage emits anything.
ordering.normalTerminal: Complete is the sole successful protocol terminal and must be followed by exit status zero and EOF with no additional byte.
ordering.unavailableTerminal: Unavailable is permitted only immediately after Analyze and before every FactBatch/Coverage frame.
ordering.budgetTerminal: BudgetExhausted is permitted after Analyze and before Complete; it terminates the entire Analyze and no later protocol frame is permitted.
ordering.cancelTransition: Cancel may be sent once from any nonterminal state; only Cancelled may follow, after which EOF is required. User-interruption D9 precedence survives a missing Cancelled caused by forced cleanup.
ordering.sequenceRule: Each direction has an independent uint64 sequence beginning at zero and increasing by exactly one. Duplicate, skipped, decreasing or overflowing sequence is provider-protocol.
ordering.unknownOrContradictory: Any frame outside these transitions, any second terminal, or any payload contradicting its phase is provider-protocol.

snapshotTransport.rule: The host streams the sealed Snapshot as a VFS. It never passes a live worktree root or asks the worker to reopen source paths.
snapshotTransport.manifest: SnapshotManifest carries SnapshotId and the complete list sorted by canonical path. Each entry commits canonical path, entry kind, byte length, content SHA-256 and, where the sealed Snapshot represents one, the sealed link target.
snapshotTransport.content: SnapshotFileChunk frames carry only bytes committed by the manifest, identified by path and monotonically increasing chunk index. SnapshotSeal commits the manifest digest and entry count. The worker validates complete byte counts and digests before SnapshotAccepted and constructs the TypeScript CompilerHost over that VFS.
snapshotTransport.packageResolution: All tsconfig graph files, program sources, package-resolution metadata, declaration files and resolved node_modules entries that contribute to the universe are snapshot/VFS entries. Runtime filesystem/module lookup outside that closure is forbidden by provider logic; incompleteness returns Unavailable with Coverage provider-unavailable.

providerProtocol.stdout: stdout is protocol-only from process start through EOF. Logs, progress, stack traces, source snippets and human diagnostics on stdout are protocol violations.
providerProtocol.stderr: stderr is a non-authoritative diagnostic byte stream captured by the host up to 256 KiB, then truncated with a host-owned marker. It never carries facts, Coverage, identity, control, terminal status or policy inputs and never changes a result by itself.

factBatchAtomicity.admitOn: valid Complete + matching stream commitments + exit status zero + EOF
factBatchAtomicity.scope: entire Analyze across every requested stage
hostValidation: FACT-PLANE factRecordContractV1 admission + FACT-ID-V1 host minting

supervision.userCancellation: On SIGINT/SIGTERM before finalization, send Cancel once, close the request side, allow the host's bounded cleanup grace, then terminate the child if needed and remove scratch. D9 class remains interrupted/130; absence of Cancelled after a user signal does not overwrite that class with a provider fault.

cleanUnavailable.coveragePayload: Unavailable.coverage contains exactly one unavailable CoverageResultV1 for every full key in every requested stage's requestedCoverageDomain.keys, in stage-major/key order
cleanUnavailable.hostOutcome: coherent Coverage-bearing Run; requiredness determines verdict, never operational-failed solely for clean Unavailable

deterministicBudget.counterRule: Counters advance only at the deterministic operations defined by ProviderWorkBudgetV1; iteration order is canonical and a provider wall clock is never read for semantic budget decisions.
deterministicBudget.wallClock: host-safety backstop only; firing kills an incomplete protocol and maps provider-protocol rather than manufacturing BudgetExhausted
deterministicBudget.coveragePayload: BudgetExhausted.coverage contains exactly one unknown CoverageResultV1 with deficiency budget-exhausted for every full key in every requested stage's requestedCoverageDomain.keys, in stage-major/key order

supervision.protocolOrCrash: A non-zero exit, signal death not caused by host user-cancellation, EOF before the terminal response, hang terminated by the supervisor, malformed output or identity mismatch is an incomplete/invalid provider protocol and maps to D9 faultCause provider-protocol / PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. No coherent Run is fabricated from partial output.
supervision.deliveryFailure: Missing, digest-mismatched or unspawnable artifacts promised by the selected signed profile map to D9 faultCause delivery-required / DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED.
supervision.success: Only a valid Complete followed by exit status zero admits the complete fact result. Extra output or a non-zero exit after Complete is provider-protocol.

authority.scratch: The host creates one private scratch directory per child with an explicit restrictive mode, passes only that path, and recursively destroys it after the child exits. Scratch is rebuildable and never evidence authority.
authority.durable: The worker cannot allocate PlanId, SnapshotId, ExecutionId or RunId; open the ledger/CAS; commit facts; seal a Run; derive policy; choose exit status; or write durable product state. Only the Rust host validates and commits returned candidates through the host store authority.
authority.source: The worker receives source and resolution inputs only through the sealed VFS protocol. It is never given a live repository root as an input contract.

environment.extraVariables: FORBIDDEN unless a later protocol major adds a closed field and PlanId classification

authority.repositoryExecution: disabled: no tsserver plugins, custom transformers, package lifecycle scripts, project hooks, arbitrary package JavaScript or native addons execute. Type declarations are data in the sealed VFS.

network.enforcementClaim: provider logic and host launch policy only; because the worker is TCB and no OS confinement profile is promised, this is not a sandbox claim

typescriptSemanticSubstrate.tcbPosture: The bundled Node.js runtime, provider JavaScript and TypeScript compiler are release-pinned TCB. The separate process contains crashes and dependency/runtime instability; it is not a security sandbox or proof of filesystem/network confinement. Stripped environment, no-addons launch and VFS-only provider logic reduce ambient inputs but do not authorize a sandbox claim without an OS-enforced confinement profile.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: embed a JavaScript engine or TypeScript compiler in the Rust host
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It crosses the selected orchestration/provider boundary and makes JS runtime crash and dependency fate part of the host process.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: use system Node.js or resolve TypeScript from the project
rejectedAlternatives.reason: It violates the exact offline release closure and makes compiler/runtime identity ambient.
It introduces cross-attempt state and an undeclared evidence authority into the one-shot v1 topology.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: one worker multiplexing several TypeScript semantic universes
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Compiler/module caches can cross-contaminate universe identity and make cleanup/failure attribution ambiguous.

distribution.installPromise: One install command selects a manifest platform row and atomically installs one complete profile. On a supported platform the default is full and provides deep TypeScript and Rust analysis offline.
distribution.updatePosture: No self-mutating updater. An explicit installer/update command verifies a new release set before atomic activation; update discovery is opt-in and off the analysis path.

platformMatrix.supportRule: Only rows in supported are release-blocking product claims. An unlisted platform is unsupported. bestEffort rows are never counted in 'supported platform' claims.

bestEffort.reason: Host toolchain is upstream tier 1, but the complete TypeScript+Rust offline bundle and release lane are not committed initially.
Static host is plausible; rustc-driver/LLVM and project native build dependencies need a separate bundle proof.

platformMatrix.releaseRule: G16 runs install, signature verification, no-network startup and one deep TypeScript and Rust fixture on every supported row for every release. A missing row result blocks release.

canonicalization.signedBytes: UTF8('opensip.release-manifest.v1\u0000') || JCS(manifest with manifestId and signatures omitted)

ReleaseManifestV1.artifactSetRule: artifacts is the exact installable set; unlisted bytes are never executed as part of the release.

ArtifactEntry.dependencyRule: dependencyIds equals the outgoing dependencyEdges for this artifact.

ProfileEntry.rule: The transitive dependency closure of artifactIds is present in the same manifest.

FormatCompatibility.fallback: readMajors and migrateFromMajors are current plus the two prior user-custody majors until evidence supports a different published window.

KeyDescriptor.publicKey: base64url without padding of the 32 raw public-key bytes

Signature.signature: base64url without padding of the 64 raw signature bytes
Signature.rule: keyId must resolve through the applicable signed RootMetadataV1 role; duplicate keyIds count once.

Role.rule: keyIds are unique and every keyId resolves in the same RootMetadataV1 keys array; threshold is positive and no greater than keyIds length.

RootMetadataV1.signedBytes: UTF8('opensip.root-metadata.v1\u0000') || JCS(root metadata with signatures omitted)

RevocationSnapshotV1.emptyState: revokedKeyIds and revokedArtifactDigests are present empty arrays and the snapshot is still threshold-signed.

VerificationPolicy.rule: offlineBundleRequired is exactly true. Root version, release role and revocation snapshot are committed by the manifest but supplied outside it, avoiding a self-containing manifest.

Trust.bootstrap: The installer/host distribution pins the initial root metadata digest. No trust-on-first-use and no network-fetched root is accepted.
Trust.rootRotation: Each new root is signed by thresholds of both the immediately previous and new roots.
Trust.revocation: A threshold-signed versioned revocation snapshot is mandatory even when its revokedKeyIds/revokedArtifactDigests arrays are empty.

OfflineReleaseBundleV1.rule: This is the install input, not a member of its own manifest. It is mandatory for every offline install; payload bytes must match every exact manifest artifact descriptor. Verification performs no network access and reports metadata age/expiry.

admissionOrder: verify root continuity and signature thresholds
verify every artifact length and digest
supplyChain.rollback: releaseSequence is monotonic. Lower is refused unless a local user explicitly forces it; a force writes a host-audit record before activation.
supplyChain.atomicity: Stage into a new version directory, verify the complete closure, fsync, then atomically switch one active-manifest pointer. Partial staging is never active.
supplyChain.offline: The verification bundle is required and sufficient; no network access and no OCSP, key, revocation or artifact fetch occurs during install or analysis.
supplyChain.provenanceInPlanId: manifestId and selected profile capabilityManifestId enter PlanId.

ProviderCapability.relationRule: Each relation key and resolution value resolves in fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry; adjectives and prose are invalid.

AbsentCapability.rule: coverageState is unavailable and deficiency is a live fact-plane value.

installProfiles.defaultRule: Every supported platform installs full by default. core remains an explicit size-minimal profile and must be affirmatively selected.

provenancePolicy.rule: One schema/capability pipeline; provenance is a typed parameter.
provenancePolicy.precedence: local-development provenance is an absolute policy-authority blocker. No override waives it.
provenancePolicy.promotion: The only route to blocking authority is a separate contribution-promotion host mutation that produces published provenance, VERIFIED state and a verificationEvidenceId, and is durably audited.

ContributionAdmission.blockingRule: role in {required,blocking} requires grant=published, signatureState=VALID, verificationState=VERIFIED and non-empty verificationEvidenceId.
ContributionAdmission.missingRule: Missing, null, false or unknown verification state is never VERIFIED.

contract.window: For format major N, the release bundles readers and idempotent previewable migrators for N, N-1 and N-2. This is the normative fallback, not an evidence-based adoption claim.
contract.legacyInspector: The same bundle contains a read-only inspector for exactly readMajors. No indefinite reader is promised.
contract.outsideWindow: Return migration-unavailable with currentMajor, readMajors, migrateFromMajors and optional bridgeBundleId. Do not claim offline usefulness outside the declared range.
contract.bridgeImport: A user may supply a signed bridge bundle by file/removable media. It is verified against the same offline root and manifest rules; the tool never fetches it.
contract.reinterpretation: Forbidden. Unknown format bytes are never parsed best-effort.

authoringDX.localLoop: A canonical local path/content digest uses the same schema and capability pipeline with local-development provenance.
authoringDX.factExploration: Bounded typed read-only query over a stored fact view; never creates a Run.
authoringDX.testKit: Fixture-based rule tests record expected evaluation outcomes and Coverage. No fixtures means UNVERIFIED/advisory.

explainTrace.retention: Tied to the Run evidence policy and diagnostic privacy/volume budgets.

policyEligibility.blocking: Only published+VALID signature+VERIFIED+verificationEvidenceId can be required or blocking.
policyEligibility.override: No override promotes local-development or UNVERIFIED code. Promotion is a distinct audited transition that creates the required evidence and provenance.
policyEligibility.visibility: grant, verificationState and verificationEvidenceId appear in Plan, Run and explain projections.

properties.property: local authoring uses one admission pipeline without publication
signed releases are exact atomic sets verifiable offline
offline compatibility holds within the declared finite window
admission does not confer policy authority
every supported platform installs the full profile and analyzes offline
DELIVERY domain conditions map into D9's closed host-termination vocabulary
the TypeScript semantic provider has one exact offline one-shot process, closed protocol-major-1 wire schema, multi-stage attribution, identity, sealed-VFS, authority and failure topology
a schema-valid external-scanner operator is rejected by the v1 overlay after mandatory RequestId ingress allocation and before attempt admission through D9's existing extension-admission outcome

assuranceStatus.rule: These are executable architecture contracts. None is QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED until G16 retains positive/negative and release executions.

conformanceTests.assert: Local-development runs with no publisher signature and is Plan-visible.
Local-development cannot be required/blocking and no override changes that.
No grant waives schema or capability validation.
Every profile is a typed capability manifest resolving exact relation rungs and Coverage.
Install/admission is atomic over exact canonical signed manifest bytes and artifact closure.
Rollback is refused or explicitly forced and audited.
Threshold/revocation verification succeeds with network denied using the mandatory bundle.
Current plus two prior majors read/migrate offline; outside returns migration-unavailable or uses a user-supplied signed bridge.
An opaque scanner reports explain UNSUPPORTED.
Blocking requires explicit VERIFIED state and retained evidence; missing/null/unknown fail closed.
G16 covers every closed supported platform with the full TypeScript+Rust offline bundle.

Every DELIVERY provider availability, budget, interruption, protocol/delivery fault or excluded-feature rejection used by the v1 slice maps through D9's live cause maps and closed public code vocabulary; domain detail never becomes a second termination vocabulary.

For each (ExecutionId, SnapshotId, TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey), the host launches one exact signed Node.js/provider/compiler closure, validates every closed protocol-major-1 envelope/payload/transition and multi-stage attribution, streams only the sealed VFS, admits facts only after Complete+matching commitments+zero-exit+EOF, destroys scratch, and never reuses worker state.

A frozen PlanIntent whose stageIntents[*] selects kind=fact-derivation/operator=external-scanner or whose contributions[*].authority is external-scanner has a host-minted reserved REQUEST-ID-V1 RequestId, then rejects during request-validation with FEATURE.EXTERNAL_SCANNER_NOT_IN_V1, no attempt/Snapshot/Plan/Run identities, and D9 extension-admission-rejected / EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED.

knownLimitations: No release candidate exists, so DELIVERY is architecture-implementable but not product-demonstrated.
The current-plus-two format window is a normative fallback; VERSIONING correctly labels its empirical grounding GUESSED.

The architecture pins the TypeScript identity mechanism and signed byte closure, not one numerical Node.js/TypeScript version forever. Each release must select and test exactly one descriptor pair per supported row; no release evidence exists yet.

Repository build scripts and proc macros may require undeclared native tools. Missing offline tools yield provider-unavailable Coverage; the product never downloads them or calls the universe complete.
The supported matrix is intentionally narrower than upstream Rust host support and may expand only with a complete G16 lane.
